questions.prompt: Your .NET 6 project needs to serialize objects to JSON without adding any NuGet package. Which library fits?
options: Newtonsoft.Json, because it ships inside the .NET runtime
System.Text.Json, because it is built in since .NET Core 3.0
Newtonsoft.Json.Linq, because it is the built-in DOM API
Neither; every JSON library in .NET needs a NuGet install
questions.explanation: `System.Text.Json` is built in (part of .NET Core and .NET 5+), while Newtonsoft.Json is an extra dependency you add through NuGet.

questions.prompt: The JSON has a `FullName` field but the class only has `Name`. What does this Json.NET code print?
options: It throws because FullName has no matching property
questions.explanation: A JSON field that doesn't match any class property is ignored, so `Name` keeps its default value (`null`) and the `??` prints `NULL`.

questions.prompt: In the lesson's `JsonSerializerSettings` example, the output is camel-cased, has no nulls and writes the enum as a string. Which setting produces the **camel-cased** property names (`firstName` instead of `FirstName`)?
questions.explanation: `CamelCasePropertyNamesContractResolver` camel-cases the names; `NullValueHandling.Ignore` drops nulls, `StringEnumConverter` writes enums as strings and `Formatting.Indented` only pretty-prints.

questions.prompt: During deserialization, which of these properties can Json.NET set from the JSON?
questions.explanation: Only public properties with a public setter can be set during deserialization; a property with a `private set` won't be set.

source.section: #### 2) Property Must Be Public with Setter

questions.prompt: You receive JSON from a dynamic API whose shape you don't know at compile time. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Deserialize it into a strongly typed class and ignore missing fields
Parse it with `JObject.Parse` and read values with LINQ-to-JSON
Write it to a `MemoryStream` and read it back with `Seek`
Mark every property of a placeholder class with `[JsonIgnore]`
questions.explanation: When the structure is unknown you can't deserialize into a typed class, so you use Newtonsoft's LINQ-to-JSON API (`JObject`, `JArray`, `JToken`) to explore and extract values dynamically.

questions.prompt: You need exactly the bytes written to a `MemoryStream`, as a new `byte[]`. Which member should you use?
questions.explanation: `ToArray()` copies the stream content to a new `byte[]`, while `GetBuffer()` returns the underlying buffer, which may include unused bytes.
